Internal

The system, on one page

Every component the site uses, rendered live rather than described. The tokens are read out of the stylesheet at build time, so nothing on this page can disagree with what ships.

On this page

Why this page existsTwelve tokensTypeButtonsPointsCardsStepsTablesFAQThe rules this stylesheet cannot survive

Why this page exists

A stylesheet nobody can see the whole of is a stylesheet everybody adds to. Four months in, that is how a site ends up with three greys that are nearly the same grey and two button heights that are nearly the same height.

So: one screen with all of it on. If a component is not here it does not exist, and if it is here and looks wrong, it looks wrong everywhere. That is the intended failure mode — this page should break first.

Twelve tokens

Read out of scene.css, chrome.css and app.css at build time. If a name here stops being defined, the build fails rather than shipping a page describing a colour nobody uses.

The site

  • --page#08090cEverything sits on this. Near-black rather than black: pure #000 makes the type look like it is floating in a hole.
  • --ink#f4f5f7Body text and headings. Off-white, for the same reason.
  • --mutedrgba(255,255,255,.62)A second voice — ledes, footer links, the text inside a card. Set in white at an alpha so it works over any surface.
  • --captionrgba(255,255,255,.48)The third and quietest: captions, field hints, eyebrows. Below this the text stops passing contrast, so there is no fourth.
  • --linergba(244,245,247,.09)Every border and rule on the site. One value, so nothing is nearly-the-same-grey as anything else.
  • --violet#8563eeThe accent. Figures, bars, focus rings, one word per headline.
  • --violet-solid#7452e6The same accent, deep enough to carry white text at 4.5:1. Buttons and the skip link only.

The product screens

  • --a-bg#ffffffThe application is light. These frames are light because it is.
  • --a-fg#1a1a1aText inside a frame.
  • --a-primary#aa8340The brass the product actually uses. Borders, accents, rules.
  • --a-primary-solid#7a5d24The same brass, deep enough for white text on top of it.
  • --a-border#eae6ddThe warm border the app draws every card with.

Points

  • A points block. Used where three or four things are true at once and none of them needs a paragraph.
  • Each item is a sentence, not a fragment — a bulleted noun tells the reader nothing they could not have guessed.
  • Four is the usual maximum. At six it stops being a list and starts being an inventory.

Cards

  • What it is

    Three or four across, each with a heading and two lines. The heading is the claim.

  • When to use it

    When the items are peers — four modules, three stages, five industries.

  • When not to

    When one item matters more than the others. A grid says they are equal.

Steps

  1. Numbered

    Where order is the point. A card grid says these are peers; steps say this one comes first.

  2. Sequential

    The number is generated, not typed, so inserting one in the middle cannot leave two threes.

  3. Finite

    Every step block on the site ends somewhere the reader can see from the first one.

FAQ

Why is this page noindex?

Because it is for whoever is building the site. It should not compete with the ERP page for a search term, and nobody arriving from Google wants a list of hex values.

What happens if a token is renamed?

The build fails. read_tokens() looks each one up by name in the stylesheet, and a missing name raises rather than rendering a blank swatch.

The rules this stylesheet cannot survive

Five. Each has been broken at least once, each took longer to find than it should have, and each fails quietly enough to ship. Three are enforced by the build; the other two are enforced by a test and by having one door.

  • 1. font shorthand may not contain inherit

    inherit is not a valid component of the font shorthand, so a browser that meets one discards the whole declaration and falls back to 16px/400 in its default family. It looks almost right, which is why this shipped twice before anyone caught it: buttons a size too large, and a textarea rendering in monospace. Use the longhand properties.

    GuardThe build greps for it and refuses to write the stylesheet.

  • 2. overflow: clip, never overflow: hidden

    hidden makes an element a scroll container. position: sticky sticks to its nearest scroll container — so one overflow:hidden on an ancestor and every sticky rail on the home page silently stops sticking, with no error and no visual clue except that the composition is wrong. clip does the same visual job and creates no scroll container.

    GuardThe build rejects overflow:hidden unless the line carries a /* sticky-safe */ marker saying nothing inside it is sticky.

  • 3. A canvas needs an explicit width

    A canvas is a replaced element, so width:auto resolves to its intrinsic bitmap width — not to the width of its container. The ambient canvas was 928 pixels wide on a 390-pixel phone, from a rule that reads correctly and is invisible on a desktop.

    GuardThe build rejects any rule whose selector names a canvas and whose block does not set a width.

  • 4. Nothing removes a focus indicator

    outline:none on a form field is the single most common way a site becomes unusable by keyboard, and it is almost always written to remove a ring the author found ugly rather than to replace it. Every interactive element on this site takes one ring, defined once. Where a field is borderless inside a shell that clips, the shell wears the ring instead.

    GuardNot build-guarded — a keyboard walk of every page checks it instead, because whether an indicator is visible is not a thing a grep can answer.

  • 5. Format, then escape — always that order

    Every string on the site goes through fmt() to fill placeholders and E() to escape HTML. Escaping first and formatting after would let a value carrying an angle bracket land in the markup unescaped, which is the shape of most template injection bugs.

    Guardesc() is the only sanctioned door and does both, in that order.
